'''Eliezer 'Leon' Ehrenpreis''' (May 22, 1930 – August 16, 2010, [[Brooklyn]]) was a mathematician at [[Temple University]] who proved the [[Malgrange–Ehrenpreis theorem]], the fundamental theorem about [[differential operator]]s with constant coefficients. He previously held tenured positions at [[Yeshiva University]] and at the [[Courant Institute]] at [[New York University]].

==Early life and education==
Leon was born in New York City to a family of Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe. He graduated from [[Stuyvesant High School]] and studied Mathematics as an undergraduate at [[City College of New York]]. Afterward, he enrolled as a doctoral student at [[Columbia University]] where he studied under mathematician [[Claude Chevalley]], obtaining his PhD in 1953 at the age of 23. His [[doctoral thesis]] was entitled "Theory of Distributions in Locally Compact Spaces".<ref>{{cite journal|title=Remembering Leon Ehrenpreis|last1=Struppa|first1=Danielle C.|date=May 2011|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=58 |issue=5|url=https://www.math.tamu.edu/~kuchment/Ehrenpreis_notices.pdf}}</ref>

==Religion==
Ehrenpreis was also a [[Rabbi]], having received his ordination from the renowned [[Rabbi Moshe Feinstein]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Eliezer 'Leon' Ehrenpreis, 80, rabbi, Temple mathematician|last=Naedele|first=Walter F.|date=September 5, 2010|newspaper=The Philadelphia Inquirer|url=https://www.philly.com/philly/obituaries/20100905_Eliezer__Leon__Ehrenpreis__80__rabbi__Temple_mathematician.html}}</ref> He was the author of a work on the [[Chumash (Judaism)|Chumash]] and other religious topics, currently in manuscript.

==Miscellaneous==
Ehrenpreis ran the [[New York City Marathon]] every year from its inception until 2007.
